0.label: fringed_bag_with_strap
0.description: A large object at the foot of the plank: an arched strap or handle above a body of striated and chequered bands, ending in a row of pendant tassels.
0.iconography: Most likely a beaded or woven bag (àpò) — a diviner's or hunter's bag — or a crown with a bead fringe. Either way, an object of office rather than a figure.

1.label: lizard_from_above
1.description: A large reptile seen from above at the top of the plank: an oval body marked with a dotted cross, four bent legs at the corners and a dotted spine that runs on down as the tail (#2).
1.iconography: A lizard or crocodile. The agama lizard appears in Yoruba origin stories and the crocodile stands for water power and royal danger (Olókun; the Benin mudfish-and-crocodile kings). Cross-culturally a guardian of thresholds.

2.label: reptile_tail_and_hatched_panel
2.description: The long dotted tail of the reptile (#1) running down the plank, beside a column of X-in-square, herringbone and diagonal hatching.
2.iconography: The tail joins the reptile to the objects below; the hatched column is woven or beaded pattern.

3.label: ring_over_fish_form
3.description: Beside the tail, a small ring above a small group of short uprights and a pointed, fish-like form marked with two lozenges.
3.iconography: Possibly a mudfish with a ring (bracelet or cowrie string) above — water and wealth — but the carving is worn.

panel.title: Ife plank: lizard or crocodile, patterned tail and a fringed bag
panel.summary: A narrow, abraded plank with a large reptile seen from above at the top, its long tail running down beside hatched panels, and a fringed bag or crown at the bottom.

register_readings.reading: A lizard or crocodile, legs splayed, with a dotted cross on its back.
Its tail running down beside hatched panels and a small ring-and-fish form.
A fringed bag or crown with a strap.

panel.composition: One long axis: the reptile's body and tail tie the top of the plank to the objects below, with pattern filling the sides.
panel.narrative: The plank pairs a powerful reptile with objects of office — a fringed bag or crown and a possible mudfish. Read with its sister planks, it may complete a set in which rulers (panel 01) and a staff-holder (panel 00) are joined by emblems of the water-and-earth powers that support kingship. The old reading took the reptile for a human figure.
panel.hypotheses: Neutral for 'chronicle' (no rulers here), but the reptile and fringed regalia fit a royal programme across the plate. Nothing clearly numerical.
cross_panel_links: Reptiles also cross the lower register of FoA_04-5578_panel_02 and the rims of the drawn trays KBA_10300 and KBA_10305.
uncertainties: The surface is heavily worn; #3 in particular is unclear.
#1 and #2 split one reptile into two boxes.
